- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- When sentiment is negative or neutral (≤ 0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is trending down.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, reduce subsequent values by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is flat (all 0.00) and model forecasts diverge significantly from true, assume mean reversion; cap forecast at 1–2 std dev above/below recent 7-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below forecast, apply downward bias correction starting from day 10–15; if above, apply upward bias from day 10–15.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 1.00, 0.33, 1.00), model may overfit short-term volatility; dampen forecast slope and use smoother trend filter.
